newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Thousands greet freed ex-President Ershad.
newsitem.headline: Thousands greet freed ex-President Ershad.

text.p: Thousands of cheering supporters greeted former Bangladesh president Hossain Mohammad Ershad with flowers as he walked from jail to freedom on Thursday.
"Justice has prevailed," shouted one as Ershad, dressed in a black suit, walked through the prison gates, smiling and waving.
"I will remain with the people," he told the crowd.
Ershad, who faced 19 charges of corruption, had been in jail since he was toppled in a people's uprising in December 1990.
His lawyers said Ershad was granted bail on Wednesday by the Supreme Court on the last of a series of corruption charges against him. It involved the purchase of defence radar equipment.
"Freedom at last," one of the lawyers told reporters. "It's the happiest moment for us."
Leaders of Ershad's Jatiya party said he would first go to the party's office and then to his home at Gulshan, near Dhaka's diplomatic enclave.
Ershad, who seized power in a 1982 bloodless coup, was sentenced to 23 years' imprisonment in four cases involving possession of illegal firearms and corruption.
The High Court last year quashed a 10-year sentence for the arms offences and Ershad has appealed against the other convictions.
Ershad had been living in a special jail set up near parliament since winning a seat in June elections.
He won bail last November, but was only allowed access to parliament, in what was the most sensational case against him -- the charge of killing Major-General Abul Manzur during a 1981 army mutiny.
Then-President General Ziaur Rahman, husband of former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia, was killed in the mutiny.
Ershad was then army chief. He deposed Zia's vice-president and successor, Justice Abdus Sattar, in the 1982 coup.
The Bangladesh Nationalist Party, headed by Khaleda Zia, described Ershad's freedom as the "outcome of a successful conspiracy" between the Jatiya Party and ruling Awami League.
Jatiya's deputy leader, Mizanur Rahman Chowdhury, said he was glad that the government of Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina "did not interfere with law and did not try to keep Ershad in prison".
Ershad's party supported Hasina's Awami League in forming a government following the June elections.
